Central bank holds rates

The central bank kept its benchmark policy rate unchanged at its August meeting, citing persistent inflation in food and transport categories and a gradual recovery in credit growth across the banking sector.

Analysts expect the stance to remain unchanged until inflation returns durably below the medium-term target. The statement noted that external demand had softened while domestic consumption remained resilient through the second quarter of the year.

The committee reiterated that future decisions will depend on incoming data, particularly the trajectory of core inflation and wage growth, and confirmed the next meeting date without signalling a change of direction.
